reviews.text: Visited the Oriental Pearl TV Tower in October 2024, and it’s easily one of Shanghai’s most iconic landmarks. Even if you don’t go up, the tower itself is impressive to see up close, especially at night when it’s fully lit and reflected along the Huangpu River. I went up to the observation decks, and the panoramic view of Pudong and the Bund is amazing. On a clear day, you can really appreciate how massive and modern Shanghai is. The glass floor section is a fun (and slightly scary) experience and worth trying at least once.

The iconic building is a feature of the Shanghai skyline from the Bund. Looks mesmerizing in the evening with glittering lights. There are observation decks if you want to visit it. We loved looking at from land from the Bund promonade, from water during our evening river cruise and from air from the top of Shanghai tower.

Iconic skyline & photo ops The area around the Oriental Pearl Tower is the heart of Shanghai’s financial district, with futuristic skyscrapers, the Huangpu River, and landmarks like Shanghai Tower, Jin Mao Tower, and the Shanghai World Financial Center. Perfect for photos, especially during sunset or at night when the buildings are lit up.

The Oriental Pearl Tower[a] is a futurist TV tower in Lujiazui, Shanghai. Built from 1991 to 1994, the tower is one of the tallest structures in China today. Its status as Shanghai's first tourist attraction, the tower's unique architecture, height, and fifteen observation decks have made it a cultural icon of the city. Since its opening, the Oriental Pearl Tower has been a cultural icon of Shanghai. The tower has been depicted in various artworks and media and attracts millions of tourists yearly.

It's an amazing view of Shanghai and the Bund up the Oriental Pearl Tower, the standard ticket is well worth it for the experience of being able to see the amazing city of Shanghai from up high. I can't give it 5 stars due to the fact that the space capsule (upper floors) were overpriced for the experience you get. The windows were incredibly small and not accessible to short people.
Just can't take enough photos of it. We were there during the day and came back at night for more photos. One of the must visit in Shanghai. Amazing tower.

It is a must visit place in shanghai.. The easiest way coming here is taking subway 1 heading Pudong airport direction, but stop at LuJiaZui. Follow the exit direction ( in mandarin), the tower just in front of you. Then taking the escalator, we arrive at beautiful round look up platform, seeing the surrounding. There are Disney Flagship store, Shanghai Ocean Aquarium. After strolling around, time to visit the tower itself.

The Oriental Pearl Tower, Shanghai 🌆✨ At night, the lights are just magical! 💖 When you look from The Bund, the tower keeps changing colors — it’s so beautiful I can’t even describe it. 😍 During the day, it’s charming in a different way. When I got closer, I was surprised at how big it actually is! I walked around taking pictures from every angle, but didn’t go up to the top this time. 📸💫

This is an important landmark that is highly recommended if you are in Shanghai. You can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view of Shanghai from above. The view from the top is even more beautiful, especially at night. The only downside is that you won't be able to see the Pearl Tower. The elevator queue can be quite long, depending on whether you visit on a weekday or a holiday. There are several souvenir shops downstairs.

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower is a striking symbol of Shanghai’s skyline, offering fantastic panoramic views of the city from multiple observation decks. Its unique futuristic design and the transparent skywalk add a fun thrill, especially on clear days. While it can get crowded and tickets are on the pricier side, the experience—especially at night when the city lights up—is well worth it either up in the tower or down below for free.

The Oriental Pearl Tower offers fantastic panoramic views of Shanghai and a fun glass-floor experience. However, it can get extremely crowded, and the waiting time is quite long — best to visit early or on a weekday. Still, it’s an iconic landmark worth seeing at least once!
One of iconic place must visit when you are going to Shanghai. The tower has glass bottom view to see 360 degree from high view.

The glass floor is a cool experience and you get great views of the city, well worth visiting if you come to shanghai. I would skip the other tower and just do this one. Also skip the little tunnel train review coming!, overall very cool just a tad expensive

One of the most remarkable building in shanghai. Ticket can be purchased if you want to go up the observatory. But you can also not purchase a ticket and just go in the lobby. Glass floor observatory is nice and offers more option to see the city and also for your photographs. Lots of stores outside the building and also at the lobby. There's also a large coke store located here. Shanghai history museum can be found here and ticket is included if you purchase the 199 rmb ticket for oriental pearl observatory.

One of the popular landmarks in Shanghai and it is highly recommended. Lujiazui financial CBD is well-designed that there is a inter-connected bridge between each surrounding buildings such as IFC, HSBC etc, providing a convenient pathway for people to walk around.

A must if visit ting Shanghai. It's a bit pricy but compared to other countries still reasonable. Views are amazing and there's so much to see. It does take time and queues take time so give yourself 3hs

The Oriental Pearl Tower is Shanghai’s oversized lava lamp, 468 meters of neon vanity project built in 1994 when architects apparently asked themselves, “How many balls can we stack before someone calls it art?” Answer: eleven. Two giant ones, nine smaller ones, and one massive identity crisis. It was once China’s tallest building, but now it stands there like the middle-aged uncle at a nightclub, insisting he was “hot stuff in the 90s” while the Shanghai Tower next door casually flexes its 632 meters of modern elegance. Inside, you’ll find a revolving restaurant spinning slowly enough to make you question both your patience and your appetite, plus a glass-floored observation deck where tourists test their courage and their bladder control at the same time. From afar, it looks like the world’s most ambitious kebab skewer. Up close, it feels like the city collectively agreed to keep this glowing disco stick because, frankly, Shanghai without it would be like New York without Times Square.. quieter, saner, but a lot less meme-worthy. The Oriental Pearl Tower isn’t just a landmark, it’s Shanghai’s embarrassing high school yearbook photo, too ridiculous to take seriously, too iconic to ever throw away.
A popular spot for taking photos. There are shopping malls around the area, and it's very convenient to get there by public transport

Visited the Tower over the weekend. Thought it would be fun but it was really packed with high volume of visitors. The queue was long, the observation halls and viewing deck was super noisy. No chance for a good photo. Thankfully we purchased the RMB399 ticket to access the Space Capsule which is the highest observation deck, situated at 351 meters. This ticket provided us the priority access to the 'lift rights' (skipped the 2 hours plus queue).
A nice alternative in comparison with the huge Shanghai Tower Good 360 degrees view but some small windows and long waiting line for the escalators

A Stunning Experience at the Oriental Pearl Tower 🌃 I visited the Oriental Pearl Tower in Shanghai at the end of February 2025, and it was truly unforgettable. The weather was quite cold, but I actually loved it — the cool air made the whole atmosphere feel calm and refreshing. The tower itself is absolutely gigantic and a total eye-catcher. You can’t help but be amazed by its unique design and impressive height. It dominates the skyline in the most elegant way! What truly took my breath away was seeing the tower at night — the lights are absolutely stunning. It glows beautifully, changing colors and standing out as one of the highlights of the city. It felt magical just being there and taking it all in. If you’re ever in Shanghai, the Oriental Pearl Tower is a must-visit — both for the amazing view and the unforgettable city vibe.

A very beautiful observation point that is worth visiting in the evening to enjoy a truly spectacular view of the city. The nighttime panorama is impressive. The staff were friendly and well organized.
visited the Oriental Pearl Tower in Shanghai it was truly unforgettable. The weather was quite cold, but I actually loved it — the cool air made the whole atmosphere feel calm and refreshing.

I visited Venus and inquired about the prices, but then I discovered that trip.com offers a better deal for the same tickets. So, make sure to check online before making a commitment. The scenery is absolutely breathtaking, especially during sunset, which is the perfect time to explore the tower. You can also visit the top level, although it may be a bit pricey. Personally, I believe the view from the second level is more than sufficient.

We visited the Oriental Pearl Tower (东方明珠塔) on a Friday afternoon, and were pleasantly surprised that the crowd was not overwhelming. The queue to enter was relatively short, making for a smooth experience. We booked our entrance tickets and revolving international buffet dinner at the revolving restaurant through Klook, which was very convenient. The tower offers a 360° panoramic view of Shanghai. Although there is an option to visit the highest sphere at an additional cost, we found the middle sphere more than sufficient to take in the stunning cityscape. Our dinner reservation was at 5pm, but a queue started forming as early as 4pm — and of course, being Singaporeans, we instinctively joined in! The buffet was decent for the price, and came with free-flow Tsingtao beer. The views were absolutely breathtaking, especially witnessing the city transform from daylight to sunset to the dazzling night skyline. Overall, it was a great experience — one we would definitely recommend to anyone visiting Shanghai.

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower is an absolute must-see in Shanghai! The tower itself is stunning — it looks like something from the future, and it lights up beautifully at night. I didn’t just visit the tower, I also took a night ferry ride on the Huangpu River, and wow… the view of the tower from the water was next-level amazing. If you’re in Shanghai, do the tower and the night ferry combo — it’s iconic and unforgettable!😍

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower is a prominent landmark in Shanghai, China, recognized for its unique, futuristic design. Located in the Pudong District, at the tip of the Lujiazui Peninsula, the tower stands opposite the historic Bund on the Huangpu River. Key Facts and Features * Height: The tower reaches a height of 468 meters (1,535 feet). When it was completed in 1994, it was the tallest structure in China until it was surpassed by the Shanghai World Financial Center in 2007. * Architecture: Designed by Jiang Huan Chen, Lin Benlin, and Zhang Xiulin, the tower's design is inspired by the idea of "large and small pearls dropping onto a jade plate." It features 11 steel spheres of various sizes connected along three columns. * Purpose: While it's a major tourist attraction, its primary function is as a radio and television tower, transmitting signals for approximately 30 television and radio stations across Shanghai. * Attractions: The tower offers a wide range of activities and sights for visitors, including: * Observation Decks: There are several observation decks at different heights, providing panoramic views of the city's skyline. The highest is the "Space Module" at 350 meters, while a lower, glass-bottomed deck at 259 meters offers a thrilling experience. * Revolving Restaurant: Located in the second-largest sphere, the revolving restaurant provides a unique dining experience with a 360-degree view of Shanghai. * Shanghai History Museum: Located at the base of the tower, this museum chronicles the city's history from its opening as an international port in 1843 to the Communist victory in 1949. * Entertainment: The tower also has a shopping center, a hotel, and even a VR roller coaster. * Illumination: At night, the tower is illuminated by a 3D light show, making it a stunning part of Shanghai's celebrated skyline.Design and Symbolism * The tower's design is more than just a series of spheres. The architects were inspired by a verse from a Tang Dynasty poem by Bai Juyi, which describes "large and small pearls falling onto a jade plate." The three large columns at the base and the spheres themselves are meant to symbolize this idea, with the tower creating a picture of "twin dragons playing with pearls falling from the sky over a plate of jade" when viewed in conjunction with the nearby Yangpu and Nanpu bridges. * The entire structure is supported by three massive diagonal columns at the base, which are 7 meters wide. These, in addition to the three vertical columns running through the center of the spheres, provide stability and a sense of dynamic movement to the design. Inner Workings and Visitor Experience * The names of the various spheres and levels within the tower are inspired by space and futurism, fitting its modern aesthetic. The highest observation deck is called the "Space Module," the lowest is "Space City," and the hotel located between the two large spheres is known as the "Space Hotel." * The tower features an impressive set of elevators. It was home to China's first double-deck elevator when it opened, a technology that increases a building's passenger capacity with fewer hoistways. The elevators can carry up to 50 people at a speed of 7 meters per second, and some even have an attendant who recites an introduction to the tower in both English and Chinese during the ascent. * The famous 259-meter-high glass-bottomed observation deck is a key highlight for many visitors, offering an exhilarating and dizzying 360-degree view of the city directly beneath their feet.

Probably the most famous tower in Shanghai..and just wait until they turn on the lights in the evening time! The view is incredible. I haven't seen anything like this in any part of the world. We didn't go up to the top of the tower but we walked around the tower and took many pictures of it. I recommend doing the river cruise at 7pm so you can see the tower change colors with the lights.
Price is around 20 €|$ for adult, the observatory (second big ball) has two floors. There is also toilet. Be careful of the weather as the fog can ruin the view.

Absolutely iconic landmark in Shanghai. Must visit. Long lines and expensive, but worth it. Situated in a very busy intersection surrounded by huge malls. Plenty of food and shopping in the vicinity. Awesome Tower!
This is an unique broadcasting tower in Shanghai. It's picturesque during night when it is lit with LED lights.

This building has amazing views during the night. Also the tower looks very pretty from the bund becoz of its unique shape it stands out from the other skyscrapers on the river side. I didn't find it worth visiting the restaurant, I felt the building from outside looks much nicer than inside

The Oriental Pearl Tower in Shanghai is an icon of the city - a landmark that cannot be missed. You can admire it from many places in Shanghai, but you can also climb to its top. Tickets cost around CNY 199 and opening hours are usually 8:00 a.m. to 10:30 p.m. The tower has several levels to offer, from the glass bridge at the top, through the observation deck and fantastic multimedia shows. From the top you can admire the panorama of the city and the Huangpu River - the views are breathtaking! At night, the tower is beautifully illuminated, creating an amazing view. An ideal place for photography lovers. I highly recommend it!

Very nice tourist spot to get a view of the greater skyline of Shanghai. Lots of people around and the wait to get in can get long especially during peak holiday season. The observation deck was neat but the floor/windows can get a bit dirty and make it hard to take good pictures.
This is a landmark building in Shanghai. We were fortunate to be staying near it. Looks beautiful at night as well .

Hard to miss!! Beautiful tower in Shanghai. Several tour packages available. I purchased full tour giving me access to uppermost view point and underground museum. Glass floor area is a must…unless you’re scared of heights! Very cool!!

If you are visiting Shanghai, you should come here to experience it. Lift takes you to the 90th floor. And once you go up the floor is transparent, which is amazing and scary too. There are two big cubes, you can go to. one is in between, the price of it for tourists is 199 RMD. And one is the top small cube. The price of it is 399 RMD.

The Oriental Pearl Tower is a well-known landmark in Shanghai and one of the tallest buildings in the world. I had high expectations for my visit, but unfortunately, the experience was not as enjoyable as I had hoped. The queue was extremely long, crowded, and pushy, which made it difficult to enjoy the experience. We attempted to purchase tickets in advance, but the official website was not very user-friendly and did not provide much helpful information. As a result, we ended up having to buy tickets on-site, near Gate 2. The atmosphere on the tower was not very pleasant. It was crowded with people, and many local visitors were sitting on the floor, blocking the walkways and creating obstacles. The tower itself appeared quite dated and in need of renovation, giving the impression of an old building. There was a deck with a glass floor area that offered a good opportunity for taking photographs, but the design of the deck obstructed most of the good views. I believe that the design could have been improved to provide better visibility.

Paris boasts the Eiffel Tower, while Shanghai features the Pearl Tower. Shanghai offers diverse attractions across multiple levels. I was particularly interested in the observation deck and glass walkway. Ticket purchase is required, and presentation of a passport or other valid identification will be necessary. The lift is rapid, and the entire experience has proved worthwhile.

It is an important landmark in Shanghai. If you buy a ticket in advance, you can scan the QR code to enter. The elevator is very fast. The queue is not long. The upper line can be seen very wide. There are food, snacks, drinking water vending machines, souvenirs, roller coasters, 5D movies. There is also a revolving restaurant, but must be booked 1 day in advance.

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower is one of the most recognizable landmarks in Shanghai, standing tall in the heart of the city’s Pudong district. This futuristic tower, with its unique design and striking presence, not only offers stunning views but also serves as a symbol of Shanghai’s rapid modernization and global stature. What immediately grabs your attention about the Oriental Pearl Tower is its unconventional and futuristic design. The tower features a series of spherical observation decks, connected by slender steel columns, giving it a bold, space-age aesthetic. The glass skywalk, suspended 259 meters above ground, is a thrilling highlight—walking on transparent flooring while looking straight down is an unforgettable experience for those brave enough to try it!

If you come to Shanghai, you must visit this place with no doubt. However, I suggest not to buy the 361m ticket. To be honest is quite dissapointing due to the exhibitions inside this level, therefore a full view of the city is not available, just very few points on small windows. Just stay at the 263m level (and below), is better and cheaper.

Shanghai Oriental Pearl TV Tower, with a height of 468 meters high is the 4th highest in Asia and the 6th highest tower in the world. Construction commenced on July 30th, 1991 and was completed on October 1st, 1994. It faces the Bund across the Huangpu River. Built with eleven steel spheres in various sizes hanging from the blue sky to the green grassland, the body of the tower creates an admirable image, which is described in an ancient Chinese verse as: large and small pearls dropping on a plate of jade(大珠小珠落玉盘).
There are a lot of shop around here, the transits was easy. The tower are great and good for photo. You can walk to the river side from here and take the view of the bund.

Excellent tourist destination in Shanghai, view from the top of the tower, the glass floor appears magnificent, particularly when the sky turns dark. I was there in summer early April. The museum in the tower depicts history and culture, which is great. If you buy your tickets ahead of time, you will save money and have a shorter wait time.
Didn’t have luck today to purchase advanced tickets to the top so we choose to walk around and take in the views from all around the Pearl Tower.

A must visit attraction when visiting Shanghai. There is an overpass where you can get closer to the tower and the other buildings in the area. It’s beautiful and it also acts as a bridge to the malls and shops.

Here’s an improved version of your description: The Perl Tower is an iconic building, best appreciated from the outside, where its striking design can be admired from multiple perspectives. No matter how many times you look at it, you always discover something new. While the interior is pleasant, a single visit inside suffices. However, the 360-degree panoramic view is truly unforgettable

I just had the most epic view of Shanghai from the Oriental Pearl Tower! Seriously, the observation deck gives you this insane panoramic view of the entire city. You can see everything from towering skyscrapers to bustling streets. It's like being in a movie! If you want to capture the essence of Shanghai's awesomeness, you've got to visit this place.

Very crowded with many people. It took 10-15 mins to get on the elevator, but the view was magnificent. Personally, I loved the view when looking down from the glass floor, which was really cool. Travelling with friends here is a good way to pass time and have a lot of fun!

I was surprised that I actually enjoyed this tourist attraction . We bought tickets that provided access to all levels including the highest level and the transparent glass walk which was the highlight of the tour. We have 360 view of the surrounding area including Lujiazhui business district and Puxi . What blew me away was the transparent glass walk which maybe daunting for those who are afraid of heights , it could make you weak in the legs . I totally love the thrill of it . For the tickets you can buy at the machines or counters . We had terrible customer service on 3 Jan 2025 at the counter , lady was totally rude .
Finally make up way up the tower after multiple trips to shanghai. Worth the view

The scenery was very nice when I came there at the end of last year (2023). The view was very nice blended with the sunset in the background. Even though visiting can cause a long walk around to and from different malls too, it is a sight not to miss. I also recommend getting down and going closer than the ring too ;)

The scenery at night is more beautiful, but it also means longer queueing and waiting. Maybe you can try to enjoy it quietly from the North Bund on the other side or enjoy an elegant dinner in the high-rise restaurant of this building without queueing up🙏

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower, located in Shanghai, China, stands as an iconic symbol of modern architecture and technological prowess. Soaring 468 meters into the sky, this remarkable structure captivates visitors with its unique design, featuring spheres and columns that resemble pearls on a string. Ascending the tower provides breathtaking panoramic views of the cityscape, including the impressive skyline along the Huangpu River. The observation decks offer a mesmerizing spectacle, especially during the evening when the city lights illuminate the surroundings. The tower's design seamlessly blends traditional Chinese elements with a futuristic touch, creating an aesthetic marvel that appeals to both locals and tourists. Beyond its visual appeal, the Oriental Pearl TV Tower houses an exhibition showcasing the evolution of technology and broadcasting in China. Interactive displays and multimedia presentations offer an educational experience, providing insight into the country's rapid development. While some critics argue that the tower's appearance might be too futuristic for its historic surroundings, the majority appreciate it as a symbol of China's progress and embrace its role in shaping Shanghai's modern identity. In conclusion, the Oriental Pearl TV Tower is not just a television broadcasting hub; it's a cultural landmark that bridges the past and present in a visually stunning way.

Pinnacle of a futuristic tower. We bought the dinner in the revolving restaurant and the Space capsule add on. The buffet style restaurant was very good with a great view. The space capsule was cool but for 100 CYN a bit steep but offered the highest overlooking view. It felt as if you were in a spaceship floating through space.
Highly recommended if you’re in Shanghai, we booked our tickets through Klook and had no issues!
Great attraction in the Bund area. It is so majestic whenever you see it from. A must stop when visiting Shanghai.

I had a great experience at the tower, I went there for the revolving restaurant experience and was blown away but the variety and quality of food. The views of the city and river was also breath taking. Definitely worth the visit. P.S the line to the restaurant floor can be very long but moves quickly. You can only by tickets for the restaurant on the actual day you're going so keep that in mind and snatch them early, they are limited.

One of the symbol of Shanghai, China I even brought a souvenir that looks like this unique tower, when I first saw this tower my can get may eyes on it, this is an icon, this is incredible!! It is photogenic in every angle. I can’t count how many times i take a picture with it lol it’s just amazing to see it pin person rather than in picture or video. Trust me it’s far better to see it personally 1 million percent!!! Its even more beautiful at night when the light show started…

Yeah this iconic place is fantastic from any point of view. No matter when or how it will hit your eyes, you will love it. The observation deck is also fantastic experience at least once. You can see the city from a different angle. During some public holidays or vacations it's super crowded so think about the ticket more in advance and everything will work great :-)

Adults 199rmb. Kids 1.2 to 1.4m half price. Kids below 1.2 free admission. Space capsule need to purchase separate tickets. Adults 100 rmb, kids 1.2 to 1.4m half price. Kids below 1.2 free admission. Personally feel the space capsule is not worth the money, there’s nothing much to be seen up there. The museum below was an eye opener showing Shanghai history in the early 1900s. Overall quite satisfied with the place but the tickets were quite pricey.
The Shanghai Pearl Tower is a futuristic landmark with stunning city views, glass observation decks, a museum, and dining options. A must-visit for tourists!
Amazing to watch from other side of river. Many colours, great view both during the day and night. Must have

We went on a weekday and there isn't a large crowd. The entrance to the tower is quite expensive as it didn't cover all the interesting levels. On the way down, they didn't allow us to take the ride all the way to the ground floor. We had to stop 3 times and were directed to take the stairs to the next elevator. This is to ensure guests pass through the game and souvenir areas. Taking the stairs down isn't suitable for seniors. Expect noisier crowd when compared to Taipei 101 and Yokohama Tower as the crowd there were not as rowdy. Walking on the glass panel is a must.

This is a pretty cool attraction. It lights up at night and it's pretty cool. I went at dusk so I was able to get a good daytime view followed by a night time view as well. I was too scared to go on the transparency deck with the glass. Hahaha! Definitely recommend going in for an hour or so!

Great tourist attraction in Shanghai, view from the top of the tower on glass floor, from the bund and river cruise in the night is awesome. The museum in the tower depicting the history and culture is fantastic. The colorful lights during the river cruise in the night is memorable. The tower stands tall and a landmark to be seen from anywhere in Shanghai.
If you look to Shanghai from this tower, it's just normal view city at night, but look from the other side to this. It generous! Busy street at night, don't have a chance to go to the top!
Must-visit for Shanghai's best views! The glass-floor walkway is thrilling. Go early to avoid crowds—100% worth it!

Awesome. The glass floor is the real attraction. Queue was about 15 minutes at 4.30pm on a Sunday which i thought was great. Booked on trip.com the same day. If your coming from the bund I recommend buying your tickets in the sightseeing tunnel they're cheaper and include the cool sightseeing metro under the river.

Fun location seriously crazy views. If you love heights this place is for you. You can see all of the Shanghai city scape from the top. The glass floor level is pretty awesome too. It can be a little jarring at first if you aren't into heights. I would get the 190 Yuan ticket. The top level is not really worth going to IMHO. It mainly details some space exploration and the windows out are small and curved. The restaurant is pretty awesome with great views and the food is buffet style - they had a Hungarian chef there also doing some ethnic dishes. Overall the food was good... For 200 ¥ it is pretty decent Overall I really enjoyed the experience.
So fun to go to the Pearl Tower and discover the view of Shanghai. It’s 200¥ to go to the top. Also the glass window passerelle is awesome.

The Oriental Pearl Tower is a futuristic landmark offering stunning views of Shanghai’s skyline and the Huangpu River. Its unique design with spheres makes it an architectural marvel. Visitors can enjoy panoramic cityscapes from observation decks, including a thrilling glass floor. The tower also houses a museum and revolving restaurant, adding to the experience. It’s a must-visit for those wanting to capture the modern essence of Shanghai.

The Shanghai TV Tower, known for its iconic design, offers a revolving restaurant with panoramic views. Visitors often enjoy the 360-degree rotation, providing a unique dining experience. While queues may be present during peak hours, the captivating cityscape of Shanghai, especially during sunset or nighttime, makes the wait worthwhile. The observation deck also offers stunning vistas, allowing visitors to appreciate the city's skyline. To fully savor the experience, it's advisable to check for potential wait times and plan accordingly, especially during popular hours.

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower in Shanghai offers breathtaking views, but my visit during the weekend was less than ideal. The crowd was overwhelming, and I endured a nearly 3-hour wait in the queue. Once I finally reached the observatory, my mood was dampened, and I only spent a quick 15 minutes taking in the view before heading down. I strongly recommend planning your visit during off-peak hours to fully enjoy this iconic attraction without the frustration of overcrowding.

Oriental Pearl TV Tower is one of Shanghai’s most iconic landmarks, located in Lujiazui, Pudong. Standing at 468 metres (1,535 ft), it was once China’s tallest structure. Its unique spherical design with 11 spheres gives it a futuristic look. The tower features multiple observation decks, including a glass-bottomed Skywalk at 259 metres, offering breathtaking city views. It also houses a museum, restaurants, and a revolving restaurant at 267 metres. A must-visit for stunning panoramas and a glimpse into Shanghai’s skyline evolution!

There are a lot of point of interest, great place to take pictures at and enjoy your afternoon to evening transition. Almost everything is clean and tidy but still you could see people smoking while walking by or even spitting on the sidewalk. Other than that, a nice place to listen to music and watching the scenery of buildings surrounding you.
Nothing too special here. Glass floor, old Shanghai museum, good view. Skip going to the highest level with the space exhibit and tiny viewing windows. Get there early.

One of the magnificent landmark of the populated city in China, the must visit city in China, you will be amazed with the tallest and ancient building plus the most beautiful scenery. Most places are crowded with people's head. This is what a big city look like.... It's really amazing and beautiful, I am lost of words. In short you need to need to be there to see it for yourself to feel the atmosphere. You will never regret and forgot what you have seen. So wait for you in Shanghai, see you there, OK?

Beautiful tower and there is more than tower inside the building, at the ground floor there are souvenirs shops and food, there is also a very interesting museum about the history of shanghai, at the middle of the tower there is a real rollercoaster! you can buy ticket for different floors. There is also a floor when you can see the city landscape and feel the wind.

Good timing to visit in the early morning. Not crowded. There was a cute orange “Mojo Carrot” on the tower, so the tower doesn’t look so lifeless lol. (Mojo carrot is designed by famous Taiwanese band’s singer “MAYDAY Ashin” and his classmate “No2good”.) You can buy the Mojo Carrot toy at the pop-up store named “STAYREAL” under the tower until early December.

Love the moment you exit from the metro(mrt) a full view of the tower and surrounding.Best part a round pedestrian walkway linking all building within a big circle.On top you can have very good photo shot of the tower We did not go up due to foggy weather.And the rate base on the level you wanted to go on top tower.

This place needs no introduction, iconic, majestic, the must see and most famous piece of Shanghai skyline. It's Sci-Fi, it's timeless, it's just unique in it's own merit. I visited during the day, didn't take anything from the experience, specially for the glass floor, which is 360° and you can see the surroundings from a very, very tall perspective. If you have only one day in the city, just come here. Crowded, whatever, it's crowded regardless.

Great place to be in the evening, right after sunset. The elevated walkway around downtown area is the best place to view the tower. This is highlight of downtown Shanghai with lots of shopping and dining options and metro nearby. Carry a jacket in winter months. Western dining options a few blocks away. Check out the photos

Iconic Shanghai landmark that everyone should pay visit to. I was there uncountable times and always finding a new views either from outside to the tower or from the tower vice versa... I recommended going there earlier in the morning than in the evening; due to the crowds... but in the evening is city simply incredible (when all lights are on).

It's just a TV tower. The tickets are very expensive and not friendly to foreign tourists. There is no English translation. There are many people on it. The scenery on the top observation deck is far inferior to other high-rise cities, even inferior to Shenzhen Diwang Building.

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower, located in Shanghai, China, is an iconic landmark and one of the tallest towers in the world. Completed in 1994, it stands at a height of 468 meters (1,535 feet) and features a unique design characterized by its distinctive "pearls" and futuristic structure. Here are some key features of the Oriental Pearl TV Tower: 1. **Design**: The tower's design is inspired by traditional Chinese architecture, with the large spheres resembling pearls strung on a necklace. The tower consists of 11 spheres of varying sizes, with the two largest spheres at the top and bottom. 2. **Observation Decks**: The Oriental Pearl TV Tower has several observation decks, including a glass-bottomed floor, providing breathtaking views of the Shanghai skyline, the Huangpu River, and the surrounding areas. 3. **Broadcasting**: As its name suggests, the tower serves as a television and radio broadcasting hub, playing a critical role in the city's communication infrastructure. 4. **Cultural Venue**: The base of the tower houses various exhibitions and a history museum, showcasing the development of Shanghai and its culture. 5. **Night Illumination**: The tower is beautifully illuminated at night, making it a stunning sight against the backdrop of the city lights. The Oriental Pearl TV Tower is not only a symbol of Shanghai's modernization but also a popular tourist attraction..

Shanghai Oriental Pearl TV Tower, with a height of 468 meters high is the 4th highest in Asia and the 6th highest tower in the world. Construction commenced on July 30th, 1991 and was completed on October 1st, 1994. It faces the Bundacross the Huangpu River. Built with eleven steel spheres in various sizes hanging from the blue sky to the green grassland, the body of the tower creates an admirable image, which is described in an ancient Chinese verse as: large and small pearls dropping on a plate of jade(大珠小珠落玉盘). The tower consists of 6 main parts: 3 gigantic columns，the 1st sphere called bottom ball(下体球)，the 2nd sphere known as upper ball(上体球),the 3rd sphere called space capsule(太空舱)， other 5 small spheres, basement and the square. There is a totally transparent panorama lift between the columns offering a quiet good view of Shanghai. This was the first wholly transparent elevator in the world. The Oriental Pear Radio & TV Tower has 3 main sightseeing floors where tourists could enjoy the city view from different heights. The Space Capsule (the 3rd sphere) is 350 meters off the ground and at 263 meters is the major sightseeing floor, the 2nd sphere. There are 2 outdoor sightseeing floors. One is 259 meters off the ground (in the 2nd sphere) and the other is 90 meters from the ground, in the 1st sphere. Tourists can visit these parts together or separately. The basement houses the Shanghai Municipal History Museum. The Oriental Pearl Science Fantasy World is located in the 1st sphere. A revolving restaurant is 267 meters off the ground, making it the 2nd highest dining area in Asia.

The Oriental Pearl TV Tower is a prominent landmark in Shanghai, China. It stands tall at 468 meters and is known for its unique architectural design featuring spheres linked by columns. The tower offers panoramic views of the city from its observation decks and has become a symbol of modern Shanghai. Additionally, it houses exhibition spaces, a revolving restaurant, and even a hotel. Visiting this iconic structure provides visitors with an opportunity to appreciate both the historical significance and contemporary vibrancy of Shanghai's skyline.

Must visit this famous tower on Shanghai's skyline. It is standing by the bank of the Huangpu River and has been the outstanding landmark of Shanghai since its completion in 1994. With a height of 468 meters, it was the tallest structure in China before 2007, now, it is the fifth highest tower in the world. Tower has fifteen observatory levels. The highest is at 351 m.
